home.heroTitle: NASA-Powered Crop Rotation & Farm Resilience in Saline Coastal Lands
home.heroSubtitle: AgriShift empowers Bangladeshi farmers with NASA Earth observation insights, soil test digitization, and climate-resilient crop rotation planning.
home.bannerNotice: Demonstration Frontend Phase: NASA data pipeline and ML inference models are currently under active development.
home.problemDesc: Over 1.05 million hectares in coastal Bangladesh suffer from seasonal salinity intrusion. Sea-level rise, erratic monsoons, and high soil electrical conductivity (EC) devastate traditional mono-crop farming. Farmers need accessible, science-backed guidance to select resilient crop sequences.
home.nasaDesc: AgriShift integrates multi-spectral satellite remote sensing data including NASA SMAP for root-zone moisture, MODIS/Landsat for vegetation indices, and GPM IMERG for precipitation accumulation to provide continuous delta-wide environmental context.
home.f1Desc: Pinpoint your farm boundaries, identify your Agro-Ecological Zone (AEZ), and track local hydrological conditions.
home.f2Desc: Upload paper soil test cards from SRDI to automatically extract pH, Salinity (EC), Organic Matter, and macronutrients.
home.f3Desc: Evaluate 25+ staple and high-value crops against seasonal soil salinity tolerance thresholds (dS/m).
home.f4Desc: Formulate 3-season crop cycles that preserve soil organic matter, reduce salt accumulation, and optimize water usage.
home.f5Desc: Simulate salinity spikes, delayed monsoons, and water shortages before investing in seeds and fertilizers.
home.f6Desc: Actionable, timely alerts for critical salinity thresholds, heat stress, and pest outbreak risks.
home.step1Desc: Select your coastal district, upazila, and field coordinates or use the interactive map.
home.step2Desc: Upload your SRDI test card or enter recent soil EC and texture measurements.
home.step3Desc: Review crops classified into Suitable, Marginal, or Risky based on local stress factors.
home.step4Desc: Adopt sustainable sequence plans that regenerate soil and maximize seasonal resilience.
home.disclosure1: AgriShift is an independent agricultural decision-support tool and is not officially endorsed or sponsored by NASA.
home.disclosure2: Satellite observations provide macro-scale regional estimates (~10-36km for SMAP, 250m for MODIS) and must be combined with ground soil tests for field-level accuracy.
home.disclosure3: Machine learning prediction modules are in validation; current recommendations rely on transparent agronomic rulebooks (BARI/BRRI/SRDI).
home.footerNotice: Built for Bangladeshi farmers, extension workers, and agricultural researchers.

dataSources.title: Satellite & Environmental Data Pipeline
dataSources.subtitle: Data provenance, sensor specifications, and Earth observation integration status.
dataSources.provenanceNotice: Frontend Data Pipeline View: Outlines the remote sensing parameters and NASA Earthdata feeds scheduled for Part 2 ingestion.
dataSources.smapParam: L3 Radiometer Surface Soil Moisture (0–5 cm)
dataSources.gpmParam: IMERG Early/Late Run Daily Precipitation Accumulation
dataSources.limitation1: SMAP microwave radiometer measures topsoil moisture (~top 5cm); sub-surface root zone requires hydrological water-balance modeling.
dataSources.limitation2: Optical satellite sensors (Landsat/MODIS) experience cloud-cover occlusion during the monsoon season (June–September).
dataSources.limitation3: Satellite observations provide macro-scale regional indicators and must be calibrated with ground-truth SRDI soil samples.

salinityPrediction.modelStatusDesc: The machine learning soil salinity inference engine is under development for Part 2/3. To maintain strict scientific integrity, no fabricated EC predictions or fake confidence scores are generated.
salinityPrediction.unitContext: Target Unit: Electrical Conductivity of Saturated Soil Paste Extract (ECe) in dS/m at 25°C.

salinityPrediction.mapLocationContext: Regional map context for the selected farm location:
salinityPrediction.mitObservedDisclaimer: Observed maps are MIT research products based on compiled and harmonized soil-salinity observations for benchmark years. They are not current measurements from your selected farm.
salinityPrediction.mitProjectionDisclaimer: These are MIT model outputs, not AgriShift predictions or field measurements. Projections use the SSP5-8.5 high-emissions scenario and provide regional context—not a measurement or forecast for an individual farm.
salinityPrediction.mitProjectionAttribution: Source: MIT Eltahir Research Group. The selected regional map is served from MIT; the interactive point lookup opens separately on MIT's site. AgriShift does not extract a value for the selected farm. Check reuse terms with the research team before redistributing this layer.
salinityPrediction.targetArchitecture: Planned Baseline Architecture: Spatio-temporal Gradient Boosted Regressor (XGBoost / LightGBM) with spatial leave-one-district-out validation.
salinityPrediction.benchmarkTarget: Target Accuracy Benchmark: MAE <= 1.2 dS/m across coastal upazilas.

modelEvaluation.title: Model Confidence & Evaluation Card
modelEvaluation.subtitle: Transparent AI model documentation, performance targets, and known limitations.
modelEvaluation.statusDesc: No trained weights are deployed in this frontend. All metrics displayed below represent design targets and benchmarking protocols defined for Part 3.
modelEvaluation.cardModelNameVal: AgriShift Delta-EC Estimator & Suitability Engine (Planned v0.1)
modelEvaluation.cardMetricRmse: Root Mean Squared Error (Target RMSE <= 1.8 dS/m)
modelEvaluation.validationStrategyVal: Spatial Leave-One-District-Out Cross-Validation (LODO-CV) to mitigate spatial autocorrelation across coastal polders.
modelEvaluation.limit1: Microwave sensor penetration is restricted to top 0–5 cm of topsoil.
modelEvaluation.limit2: Monsoon cloud obscuration affects optical NDVI readings between June and September.
modelEvaluation.limit3: Local river salinity surges during neap tides cannot be detected from space without tidal gauge calibration.
